focusQuestion: What is the strongest first cryopreservation wedge in islets, and what evidence would justify a real entry point?

activeWedge.title: Additive-assisted islet recovery benchmark on a fixed base cryomix
activeWedge.claim: Several islet papers imply that recovery gains may come from adjuncts added around a standard cryomix rather than from entirely new base CPA chemistry.
activeWedge.currentRead: Best current wedge in islets. The literature is strong enough to justify a focused additive benchmark, but not strong enough to claim a winning adjunct yet.
activeWedge.recommendedNextStep: Run a fixed-backbone additive benchmark with p38 MAPK inhibitor, Trehalose, Beraprost Sodium, Polyvinyl Pyrrolidone on a DMSO-centered base mix, using post-thaw function as the primary readout.

standardPattern.explanation: Current default literature center of gravity is slow-freezing, usually built around Dimethyl Sulfoxide, Sucrose, Ethylene Glycol in islets, pancreatic islets workflows. Normalized workflow signal is cooling -> storage, cooling -> warming, loading -> cooling, with repeated condition mentions such as Dimethyl Sulfoxide 2 M, Dimethyl Sulfoxide 1 M, Dimethyl Sulfoxide 0.67 M.

protocolFamilies.interpretation: Most common preserved workflow in-slice, centered on Dimethyl Sulfoxide, Sucrose, Ethylene Glycol. Outcome emphasis is viability, function, transplantation, suggesting this is the baseline to beat rather than the frontier.
Smaller but sharper cluster, often tied to Dimethyl Sulfoxide, Ethylene Glycol, Sucrose. This is the likely optimization frontier if post-warm outcomes can be made more comparable.
Direct comparison slice is small (1 papers) but high-value because it anchors head-to-head decisions instead of isolated protocol claims.

opportunityScan.title: Matched-species islet vitrification vs slow-freezing benchmark
opportunityScan.whyInteresting: The current islet corpus overweights slow-freezing, so a matched-species comparison is needed to separate real vitrification gains from endpoint and species confounding. Evidence papers=6, strong outcomes=4, contradictions=20.
opportunityScan.painPoint: Vitrification and slow-freezing remain confounded by species and endpoint differences.
opportunityScan.commercialWhyNow: A cleaner benchmark wedge maps to transplant and cell-banking workflows where protocol uncertainty still blocks standardization.

opportunityScan.title: Promote islet function-heavy protocols to transplantation endpoints
opportunityScan.whyInteresting: Several islet protocols that look promising on insulin secretion or in-vitro function will reorder once they are compared on graft or transplantation outcomes. Evidence papers=6, strong outcomes=4, contradictions=10.
opportunityScan.painPoint: Promising protocols are still over-indexed on viability or in-vitro function rather than transplantation-grade outcomes.
opportunityScan.commercialWhyNow: Moving from viability-only claims to transplantation/function claims is what makes an optimization story commercially credible.

opportunityScan.title: Full-text protocol resolution for sparse islet thaw/loading workflows
opportunityScan.whyInteresting: A small number of islet papers still look interesting, but their step structure is too thin to compare fairly against the rest of the corpus. Evidence papers=6, strong outcomes=3, contradictions=1.
opportunityScan.painPoint: A small number of promising papers still lack enough procedural detail to compare fairly.
opportunityScan.commercialWhyNow: This is close enough to real preservation workflows that better protocol evidence could matter commercially, not just academically.

opportunityScan.title: Scale-up benchmark for banked or bulk islet handling
opportunityScan.whyInteresting: Scale-up losses in islet banking may come from handling and thaw workflow variance rather than core cryomix choice alone. Evidence papers=3, strong outcomes=3, contradictions=10.
opportunityScan.painPoint: 10 unresolved contradictions remain in the relevant evidence slice
opportunityScan.commercialWhyNow: A cleaner benchmark wedge maps to transplant and cell-banking workflows where protocol uncertainty still blocks standardization.
